TASK: The assembler was opening a shrink wrapped bundle of cartons on the packing bench. The task was being done while behind the plan or a deadline. Stage of the task: in process - normal running work. Method in effect: No written procedure exists for this task. No written procedure exists for this task. Equipment involved: Utility knife with a retractable blade from the tool crib. Equipment state at the time: at rest or stopped. Equipment condition: worn, dull or near end of life. Detail: The blade had not been changed for several weeks and was noted as dull. The object handled weighed 10 to 25 lb. Handling difficulty: bulky - hard to get arms around and no hand holds. It was held one hand and wearing gloves that affected the grip. PPE in use: safety glasses and general purpose gloves. This differed from the PPE specified for the task.

SEQUENCE: The event was witnessed by at least one other person. Immediately before the event: standing at the packing bench with the bundle at waist height, left hand flat on top of it and the knife in the right hand about 6 inches away. Body position at the moment: standing upright. At the moment of the event: the blade cut through the wrap sooner than expected, the knife continued travelling toward the body, and it contacted the left index finger resting on the wrap. Immediately after the event: the knife was set down on the bench, the cut was covered with the right hand, and the team lead was called over.

MECHANISM: Mechanism: The knife blade was moving toward the body and the left index finger was stationary on the bundle. It travelled under 1 foot. The object weighed under 10 lb. Point of contact: palm side of the left index finger at the middle joint. Force applied toward the body.

CONDITIONS: Difference from a normal run of this task: The dull blade needed more force than usual, which is why the cut released suddenly. Conditions at the point of injury: time or production pressure. Detail: The packing line was running behind and cartons were being opened faster than normal. The event occurred in the second half of the shift. No overtime was being worked. It happened within the first few minutes. The assembler had performed this task before. A known hazard, prior near miss, open action or risk assessment covers this task. Detail: Cutting toward the body has been raised at two toolbox talks and safety knives were requested for this bench about three months ago. A guard, interlock, barrier or control was bypassed, missing, defeated or ineffective. Detail: A self retracting safety knife is the specified control for this bench but none were available in the tool crib. Stop-work opportunity: The employee could have waited for a safety knife to be issued, but that would have stopped the packing line for an unknown period.

IMMEDIATE ACTIONS: At the scene, the wound was rinsed or irrigated and a sterile dressing was applied. Detail: Pressure applied for about five minutes to control bleeding. This was given by a trained first aid responder. Notified: the team lead and EHS. This happened within a few minutes. Afterwards, the scene was left undisturbed for EHS. Work at the location stopped. The assembler was sent to an offsite occupational clinic for evaluation.
